source_text: Qui de ecclesia sumus Moysen recipimus ut prophetam figuris futura scribentem. Iudaeus litterae prophetam negat.
thought_title: We receive Moses as prophet of figures; the Jew denies the prophet of the letter
orientation: Origen opens the homily by contrasting the Church's reception of Moses as a prophet writing future things in figures with the Jew's denial of the prophet of the letter.
pass_a_gloss: We who are of the church receive Moses as a prophet writing future things in figures. The Jew denies the prophet of the letter.

choices.english: We who are of the church
choices.why: Keeps the relative clause structure and the ecclesia glossary term; 'of the church' preserves the partitive sense of de.
rejected: Those of us in the church

choices.why: Preserves the instrumental force of figuris and the glossary term 'figure'; 'future things' renders the neuter plural futura as a substantive.
Keeps the genitive litterae as 'of the letter' with the glossary term 'letter', showing the Jew's reduction of Moses to the literal sense.
rejected: the prophet according to the letter

pass_b_english: We who are of the church receive Moses as a prophet writing future things in figures. The Jew denies that he is the prophet of the letter.

last_rejected.quote: The Jew denies that he is the prophet of the letter
last_rejected.why: English says Jew denies Moses is prophet of letter; source says Jew denies prophet of letter (i.e., rejects the letter's prophet/Moses as prophet). Ambiguous but 'negat' takes accusative: Jew denies/rejects the prophet of the letter.
last_rejected.fix: The Jew rejects the letter's prophet.
last_rejected.ruling: 'litterae prophetam negat' = denies he is prophet of the letter; accusative with 'negat' supports English rendering. No meaning change.
